tax.heading: Provision in Lieu of Income Taxes
tax.text:
Our tax sharing agreement with Oncor Holdings, Texas Transmission and STH provides for the calculation of amounts related to income taxes for each of Oncor Holdings and Oncor substantially as if these entities were taxed as corporations and requires payments to the members determined on that basis (without duplication for any income taxes paid by a subsidiary of Oncor Holdings).

We are a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes. Accordingly, while partnerships are not subject to income taxes, in consideration of the presentation of our financial statements as an entity subject to cost-based regulatory rate-setting processes, with such costs historically including income taxes, the financial statements present amounts determined under the tax sharing agreement as “provision in lieu of income taxes” and “liability in lieu of deferred income taxes”. Such amounts are determined in accordance with the provisions of the accounting guidance for income taxes and accounting standards that provide interpretive guidance for accounting for uncertain tax positions and thus differences between the book and tax bases of assets and liabilities are accounted for as if we were a stand-alone corporation.

net.text: The fair value of an interest rate derivative instrument is recognized on the balance sheet as a derivative asset or liability and changes in the fair value are recognized in net income if the criteria for cash flow hedge accounting are not met or if the instrument is not designated as a cash flow hedge.

ocf.text: Depreciation and amortization expenses reported in operating activities in the statements of consolidated cash flows were $173 million and $139 million more than the amounts reported in the statements of consolidated income in 2024 and 2023, respectively . The differences are due to certain regulatory asset amortization being reported as operation and maintenance expense in the statements of consolidated income in accordance with GAAP.

da.text: Depreciation and amortization increased $82 million to $1.060 billion in 2024. The increase was primarily attributable to ongoing investments in property, plant and equipment and higher depreciation and amortization rates as a result of implementing the final order in PUCT Docket No. 53601 in 2023. We expect depreciation and amortization to continue to increase, particularly given our capital expenditure plans. See “—Financial Condition—Liquidity and Capital Resources—Available Liquidity and Liquidity Needs, Including Capital Expenditures—Capital Expenditures” for more information on our five-year capital plan.

wc.heading: Accounts Receivable – Net
wc.text:

The accounts receivable balance from REP subsidiaries of our two largest customers, collectively represented 22 % and 19 %, respectively, of our accounts receivable balance at December 31, 2024 and 22 % and 20 %, respectively, of the accounts receivable balance at December 31, 2023. No other customer represented 10% or more of the total accounts receivable during such periods.

Under a PUCT rule relating to the Certification of Retail Electric Providers, write-offs of uncollectible amounts owed by REPs are deferred as a regulatory asset.

See “Item 1A. Risk Factors—Risks Related to Our Business and Operations— Severe weather, natural disasters and other related phenomena have in the past and could in the future have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flow, and climate change could make such phenomena more prevalent and unpredictable ” for discussion of the potential impact significant storms could have on our business. Storm related costs are generally recorded as a regulatory asset and our ability to recover any amounts included in those regulatory assets in rates as well as the time period for such recovery is subject to PUCT review and approval.

net sales.heading: Revenue Recognition
net sales.text: Oncor’s revenue is billed under tariffs approved by the PUCT and the majority of revenues are related to providing electric delivery service to consumers. Tariff rates are designed to recover the cost of providing electric delivery service including a reasonable rate of return on invested capital. Revenues are generally recognized when the underlying service has been provided as prescribed by the related tariff. See Note 3 for additional information regarding revenues.

intro.text: Headquartered in Dallas, Oncor is a regulated electricity transmission and distribution business that uses superior asset management skills to provide reliable electricity delivery to consumers. Oncor (together with its subsidiaries) operates the largest transmission and distribution system in Texas, delivering electricity to more than 4.1 million homes and businesses and operating more than 145,000 circuit miles of transmission and distribution lines in Texas. While Oncor is owned by two investors (indirect majority owner, Sempra, and minority owner, Texas Transmission Investment LLC), Oncor is managed by its Board of Directors, which is comprised of a majority of disinterested directors.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
